quote: I said I need to buy a house. It's time to figure out what I'm doing. I don't have money to put solar in my house.
stewart_read: This is a direct 'can't afford it' style objection landing in the first 20 seconds; the schema's flip ('what you can't afford is your current bill') was available and unused.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically holding back to first re-establish legitimacy given the customer disputes even requesting the call — but rep never returns to address the affordability line at all.
coaching_implication: Rep should flip to bill-pain framing immediately rather than letting the objection sit unaddressed while customer keeps talking.

stewart_read: This is a hello-objection/not-interested statement inside the first 30-40 seconds; the correct move is acknowledge + 30-second small ask, not a filler 'Gotcha, gotcha' followed by a pricing pitch.
coaching_implication: Train the rep to recognize 'leave me alone' as the hello_objection trigger and run the small-ask template instead of pivoting into cost defense.

stewart_read: Repeated 'gotcha' filler with no substantive response reads as the rep stalling rather than steering, right after the customer's most hostile line.
coaching_implication: Replace filler acknowledgments with a specific reframe or question that moves the call forward.

quote: Yeah. I mean, the only free part, Mustafa, is we take care of the installation fee
stewart_read: Rep explains financing mechanics (installation fee, no down payment, bill elimination) unprompted, which is closer-tier content the setter shouldn't be litigating on a hostile, unverified lead.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be trying to counter the customer's 'it's not free' skepticism directly, which is a legitimacy question rather than pure scope creep.
coaching_implication: Redirect to the specialist for financing detail instead of explaining the payment structure himself.

stewart_read: Rep states 650 as the threshold; schema's documented threshold is 670, matching the same drift already flagged in SESSION18_fcbf33c1 — this is a floor-wide numbers inconsistency, not this rep's error alone.
coaching_implication: Flag for Kenny reconciliation on the live credit threshold; rep is likely repeating what he was trained, not freelancing.

quote: Gotcha. So where are you at currently? I'm so sorry.
stewart_read: After the customer confirms he fails the credit qualifier — a hard DQ — the rep tries to ask an unrelated question rather than closing the call cleanly or bridging to an alternative path, confusing the customer into hanging up.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have been attempting a soft callback offer ('reach back out in a couple months') that got cut off by this stray question, which would be a legitimate procedural move rather than a pure error.
coaching_implication: On a hard DQ, close cleanly: acknowledge, offer the future-callback path clearly, and end — don't introduce a new open-ended question.
